summary: PWA Scanner Staff (FREK CC2026) tested end-to-end. Backend: 19/19 pytest passed (login matrix, /me, zones, marchands permission, badge lookup, walk-in emit + idempotency, access scan + chain notarize, cashless payment with real recharge, sync replay permission matrix, PWA assets, notary regression). Frontend: 100% pass — all data-testids present, redirect /scan -> /scan/login works, ACCES-01/2222 sees only mode-access enabled, SUPERVISEUR-01/9999 sees all 3 modes enabled, CASHLESS-01 cashless page renders all controls (marchand-select, montant-input, quick-1/2/5/10, pay-btn) and quick-5 correctly fills montant=5, EMISSION-01 emit form renders all fields, /scan/queue empty state renders with disabled flush-btn. PWA manifest + service worker served HTTP 200. One latent backend bug found (non-blocking via UI).

minor.issue: WalkinEmitRequest.type_badge has Pydantic default 'PARTICIPANT' which is NOT in badges.nomenclature.BADGE_TYPES (valid types: ART/INT/STF/BNV/PRS/VIP/OFF/SPO/EXP-*). Calling /scan/emit without type_badge -> 400. Frontend always sends a valid value via emit-type <select> (default BNV) so this never surfaces in UI flow, but the API contract default is broken. Fix: change default to 'BNV' (or any valid key) in /app/backend/staff/scan_routes.py:WalkinEmitRequest.

issues: Native browser <select> used for emit-type (TYPE BADGE). Acceptable for mobile PWA (better mobile UX than custom dropdown), but inconsistent with shadcn UI used elsewhere in app.

action_items: Optional: in /app/backend/staff/scan_routes.py change WalkinEmitRequest.type_badge default from 'PARTICIPANT' to a valid key (e.g. 'BNV'). Low priority — UI never relies on the default.
critical_code_review_comments: scan_routes.py: WalkinEmitRequest default 'PARTICIPANT' is not a valid BADGE_TYPES key — see minor issue above.
scan_routes.py: _notarize swallows all exceptions silently (warning log only). Acceptable for fire-and-forget but accumulating notarize failures will not surface anywhere actionable.

scan_routes.py: scan/access does not idempotency-check on (badge_id, zone, agent_id, day) — a double-tap will create 2 scan rows + 2 EMISSION stages for SCENE/VIP/BACKSTAGE. Sync replay can amplify this. Consider client_uuid dedupe on db.scans.

scan_routes.py: /scan/sync trusts client_uuid only as a label; there's no dedupe by client_uuid against past inserts -> a flaky network can replay the same action and double-debit jetons or double-create badges (walk-in is email_hash idempotent so emit is OK, but access + cashless are NOT). Recommend: store client_uuid on scans/transactions and reject duplicates inside _resolve+sync.

routes.py: PIN hashing uses SHA-256 with a salt from env. For 4-digit PINs this is vulnerable to rainbow table even with salt — consider bcrypt or argon2 for the staff_pin_hash field. Low risk because auth surface is small + tokens rotate every 8h.
Frontend ScanLogin: PIN field accepts up to 6/8 digits but no UI cap shown — visually OK as buttons disable after 6.
PWA: scan-sw.js is served and manifest is reachable. Did not test offline cache strategy (out of headless test scope).
